transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... honestly, I'm just having a very hard time functioning right now. It all started since my wife's fall. I've always been the man with the lists and the plan, but lately... I just sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I end up crying, or snapping over absolutely nothing. And everything else is just piling up—the bills, my mentoring calls, even basic housework. It's like I just can't make myself do any of it anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way since your wife's fall?
It's been about two months now. That's when she had the fall, and... well, that's when everything at home just completely changed. I've been feeling this way ever since.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I'm not really sure. I haven't exactly tried to do anything for fun lately. I just... I haven't had the time or energy to even attempt my usual hobbies since she got hurt, so I don't really know if I'd enjoy them or not right now.
Do you feel guilty about anything related to your wife's fall?

Guilty? No, not really. I mean, it was just an accident. She slipped, and there was really nothing I could have done to prevent it. So I don't blame myself for the fall itself, if that's what you're asking. It's just... managing everything after the fact that I can't seem to handle.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Well, like I was saying a minute ago... I haven't really tried doing any of them. Between taking care of her and managing the house, there just isn't any time for me to even think about my old hobbies. So I don't know if I've actually lost interest, I just... haven't even attempted to do anything like that since she got hurt.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad most of the day. It's not really sadness... I'm just incredibly overwhelmed. I don't sit around crying or feeling down in that way, I just feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water with all the new responsibilities right now. So, no, not sad. Just stressed.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing that you've actually tried to do since your wife's fall, but found you didn't enjoy as much as you used to?

No, not at all. Like I mentioned a moment ago, I haven't actually tried to do any of them. There just hasn't been a chance to even attempt my old hobbies with everything going on. So... I can't really say if I'd enjoy them less, because I just haven't done them, period.
Have you noticed a decrease in the pleasure you derive from activities you still manage to do, like everyday tasks or interactions with others?

No, I can't say that I have. Everyday tasks are just... well, they're just chores. I never really got much pleasure out of doing the laundry or grocery shopping to begin with, so that hasn't changed. And as for talking to people, I still appreciate it when friends or our kids call. It's just that most of our interactions are basically updates about my wife's recovery right now. So, no, I wouldn't say I enjoy those things less. Everything is just very functional at the moment.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since your wife's fall?

No, my weight has been pretty steady. I haven't noticed any significant change, up or down, since the fall. I mean, I'm still eating my regular meals, just... maybe rushing through them a bit more these days. But no, no real change in my weight.
Do you feel tired most of the time?

No, I wouldn't say I feel tired most of the time. I mean, I'm certainly busy, and there's a lot on my plate with taking care of things around the house and helping my wife, but... I'm not physically exhausted or anything like that. I still have the energy to get through the day and do what needs to be done. So, no, fatigue hasn't really been an issue for me.
Have you been feeling anxious most of the time since your wife's fall?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious most of the time. I mean... obviously, I'm concerned about her recovery and making sure she's okay, but I'm not sitting around feeling panicked or on edge all day. It's more just being focused on what needs to get done right now. So, no, I don't feel anxious.
Have you been feeling worthless or having thoughts that you're not a good person since your wife's fall?

No, I don't feel that way at all. I mean, I know I'm doing the best I can to help her and manage everything around here. I don't have any thoughts about being worthless or a bad person. I'm just a husband trying to take care of his wife after an accident. So, no, nothing like that.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite since your wife's fall?

No, not really. My appetite is pretty much the same as it always is. I mean... I'm the one doing most of the cooking right now, so maybe the meals are a little simpler than what my wife usually makes, but I'm still eating my regular amounts. I haven't lost my appetite or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future or your wife's recovery?

No, I don't think I'm worrying about the future all the time. I mean, of course I want her to get better, and we take it day by day with the physical therapy and all that. But I'm not sitting around agonizing over what's going to happen next month or next year. I'm just dealing with what's in front of me right now. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm often worrying about it.
Do you feel like you're in a low mood for most of the day, even if you said you don't feel sad?

No, I wouldn't say I'm in a low mood, either. I mean... I'm just busy doing what needs to be done around the house. I'm not walking around feeling down or gloomy all day. It's just a lot of work right now, but it doesn't put me in a bad mood. So, no, I don't feel that way.
Have you tried to do something you used to enjoy since your wife's fall and found that you didn't enjoy it as much as you used to?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, I haven't really had as much free time for my usual hobbies lately because of all the extra work around the house. But on the occasions when I do get a minute to sit down with a good book or watch a game, I still enjoy it just as much as I always did. So, no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities since your wife's fall?

Yes, I suppose I have been avoiding some things. I mean, I've just stopped showing up for my mentoring and community commitments. I just can't seem to get there right now. And it's not just that... things I used to handle without even thinking about them—like the bills, keeping up with the house, just basic household routines—they're slipping badly. I'm just not keeping up with any of it the way I used to.
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities because they remind you of your wife's fall?

No, it's not because they remind me of the fall. I mean, the bills and the house have nothing to do with that. It's just... I don't know, I just can't seem to manage them right now. It's not about avoiding reminders, I just don't have it in me to keep up with it all.
Did your wife's fall and its aftermath feel traumatic to you?

No, I wouldn't use the word traumatic. It was stressful, certainly, and it's turned our lives upside down with all the extra care she needs and the physical therapy and everything. But it wasn't a trauma in that sense. It was just an accident, and now we're dealing with the fallout.
